questions.stem: What does an Apache Airflow job in Fabric give a team?

options.text: A KQL database for storing and querying event data from scheduled workflow runs
A managed Apache Airflow environment for authoring and running DAGs written in Python
A low-code Power Query editor for building scheduled transformations without writing Python
A deployment pipeline with Airflow branding that promotes items between stages

questions.explanation: An Apache Airflow job hosts Airflow for you, so the team writes DAGs in Python and runs them without managing the Airflow infrastructure.

questions.stem: Airflow DAGs in a workspace are scheduled to run through the night. Which pool choice keeps them running on time?

options.text: A custom pool, which can stay on
The starter pool, which shuts down after a period with no activity
No pool; Airflow jobs don't use compute
A Spark starter pool

questions.explanation: The starter pool suits development and stops when idle. Scheduled production DAGs need a custom pool that stays available.

questions.stem: In which language do you write the DAGs an Apache Airflow job runs?

options.text: T-SQL
KQL
Python
Power Query M

questions.explanation: Airflow DAGs are Python files that define tasks and their dependencies.

questions.stem: Which two are configured in a workspace's data workflow (Apache Airflow) settings? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: The capacity SKU
The sensitivity label of every item
The workspace's Git provider
The custom pool's compute size
Whether jobs use the starter pool or a custom pool

questions.explanation: The data workflow settings choose the pool and, for a custom pool, its size and scaling. Git, labels and capacity are set elsewhere.

questions.stem: A developer uses the starter pool for Apache Airflow jobs and leaves the environment idle for 30 minutes. What has happened to the Airflow runtime?

options.text: It was converted to a custom pool, which stays on until someone pauses it
It was deleted together with its DAGs, which must be uploaded again
It is still running and billing, since starter pools never shut down on their own
It shut down after 20 minutes of inactivity and takes up to 5 minutes to resume

questions.explanation: The starter pool shuts down after 20 minutes of inactivity, and resuming takes up to 5 minutes. Custom pools stay on until paused.

questions.stem: A custom Airflow pool can't run enough DAGs at the same time. Which pool property adds capacity for more concurrent DAGs?

options.text: Startup latency
Extra nodes
Pool name
Default environment

questions.explanation: Extra nodes let the pool run more DAGs concurrently, and each one adds capacity for three more workers.

questions.stem: You create a custom Airflow pool for simple DAGs that run a few lightweight tasks. Which compute node size does the guidance suggest?

options.text: XX-Large
Large
X-Large
Small

questions.explanation: Airflow pools offer Small for simpler DAGs and Large for complex or production DAGs.

questions.stem: Put the steps to switch a workspace's Airflow jobs from the starter pool to a new custom pool in order.

options.text: Select Create
Expand Default Data Workflow Setting and select New Pool
In the Data Factory section, select Apache Airflow Runtime Settings
Set the name, compute node size, autoscale and extra nodes
Open the workspace settings

questions.explanation: The custom pool is created from the workspace's Apache Airflow runtime settings by choosing New Pool in the default data workflow setting, configuring it, then creating it.

questions.stem: A workspace admin turns off the setting that lets items customize compute configurations. Which pool do Apache Airflow jobs in the workspace use?

options.text: No pool, so Airflow jobs fail to start until it is turned on
The starter pool, for all environments in the workspace
The workspace's default Spark custom pool for notebooks
The last custom pool created by any workspace admin

questions.explanation: With item-level compute customization turned off, the starter pool is used for all Airflow environments in the workspace.

questions.stem: A team's Apache Airflow job runs one Airflow version and they need a different version. What should they do?

options.text: Create a new Apache Airflow job with the version they want
Change the version in the workspace's Airflow runtime settings
Upgrade the version from a DAG file
Change the version in the job's settings

questions.explanation: You can't change the Airflow version of an existing job. You create a new job with the version you need.
